prBodyNotes: {{#if isVulnerabilityAlert}}🔒 **Security fix**: no stability window{{#if (or isMajor (equals manager 'github-actions'))}}, but {{#if isMajor}}it is a major update{{else}}GitHub Actions updates are never merged automatically{{/if}}, so it waits for a manual merge{{else}}; it automerges on green CI{{/if}}.{{else if (includes labels 'automerge')}}{{#if (containsString packageName 'mbologna/')}}{{else if isMinor}}📅 **Automerges** once its stability window has passed (14 days by default for a minor update).{{else if isPatch}}📅 **Automerges** once its stability window has passed (7 days by default for a patch).{{/if}}{{else if (equals updateType 'lockFileMaintenance')}}👤 **Manual merge.** npm and Poetry lock files (and uv.lock where the repository sets exclude-newer) resolve only releases at least 7 days old; other lock files take whatever is newest.{{else if isMajor}}👤 **Manual merge.** A major update: it waited 30 days for others to report breakage; read the release notes before merging.{{else if (and (equals manager 'pre-commit') (equals updateType 'digest'))}}👤 **Manual merge.** The hook's release tag now points at a different commit, which is how a hijacked tag looks: find out why before merging.{{else if (equals manager 'github-actions')}}👤 **Manual merge.** GitHub Actions updates run with this repository's permissions, so they are never merged automatically.{{else}}👤 **Manual merge.** A rule in the Renovate config holds this update for review.{{/if}}

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: CVE-triggered PRs (OSV/GitHub Advisory on a version you use): add security label, fix(security): prefix, bypass age gate and schedule. No automerge setting here: Renovate applies this block as force, over every packageRule, so automerge: true overrode the never-automerge rule for GitHub Actions and the manual review of majors. Patch and minor fixes still automerge on green CI through the update-type rules. 1-minute floor (not 0 days) ensures Renovate posts a stability check — 0 days normalises to null internally, no check is posted, and GitHub returns state: pending with empty statuses which blocks automerge on repos without CI. timestamp-optional because CVE fix packages may lack a releaseTimestamp. Being force, its labels replace the automerge/manual-review label every rule sets; the top-level addLabels template puts it back for CVE fixes, restating which fixes the update-type and GitHub Actions rules keep from automerging, the one place the preset has to. commitMessageSuffix is emptied: Renovate's default [SECURITY] only repeated the fix(security): prefix and the security label.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly refresh of every lock file to the newest versions the ranges allow, transitive ones included. Renovate posts no stability check for it, but hands minimumReleaseAge to two package managers: npm install --before=<now minus 7 days> and Poetry's POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE, so npm and Poetry lock files take only releases at least 7 days old (the former 1 minute made that gate a no-op). Every other lock file (composer, cargo, bundler, ...) takes whatever is newest, and uv.lock too unless the repo sets [tool.uv] exclude-newer (which uv lock honours; the uv consumers set 7 days), so it must not automerge: with automerge it merged unaged transitive releases within hours in every repo with a lock file (thelounge-plugin-apprise-push #55, #68, #76). A person merges it. timestamp-optional because the update has no release timestamp, so with the default the branch would stay pending.

dockerhub-suffix.description: Docker Hub tags for images with more than 1,000 tags, where the docker datasource loses every release timestamp (see the packageRules that use it). One page, newest first, filtered to tags containing the pinned tag's suffix (3.12-alpine -> name=-alpine, 28-dind -> name=-dind), so the variants that matter are on it. Carries the per-tag digest: Renovate takes newDigest from the release, so tag@digest pins keep working, including same-tag digest updates. packageName is the Docker Hub repository (library/python).

customManagers.description: Hugo version passed to the reusable Hugo workflows (hugo_version: input in callers, default: under the hugo_version input here). The hugo-version: input of peaceiris/actions-hugo is already handled by the built-in github-actions manager with the same depName, so every Hugo pin lands in one PR.

OpenTofu version passed to the reusable terraform-ci workflow (opentofu_version: input in callers, default: under the opentofu_version input here). Without it the pins went stale unseen (k3s-oci and the default sat at 1.9.1 while 1.13 was current). The depName joins the existing opentofu group, so every OpenTofu pin moves in one PR.

packageRules.description: Major updates: hold 30 days to let the ecosystem surface breaking changes and incompatibilities, then assign for manual review — no auto-merge
Patch and pin updates: hold 7 days to let the community catch supply-chain attacks before auto-merging on green CI

Digest and pinDigest updates: 1-minute floor forces Renovate to post a stability check. 0 days normalises to null internally (no check posted = branch stays pending forever on repos without CI). timestamp-optional required because a digest update's branch carries no releaseTimestamp (the lookup-level gate ages it against its tag's latest release where the datasource gives dates, but that date never reaches the branch) — with the default 'require' behaviour the branch stability check would stay PENDING forever regardless of how many times Renovate runs. internalChecksAsSuccess handles repos without CI.

Third-party image digests (base-image rebuilds): Renovate ages a digest update against its tag's latest push (lookup applyMinimumReleaseAgeToDigestUpdate), so a short gate works where the registry gives dates (Docker Hub via the docker datasource, custom.dockerhub-suffix); ghcr/quay digests have no date and still pass (timestamp-optional). 2 days stays below the weekly-or-slower rebuild cadence of official images. pinDigest stays at the 1-minute floor: pinning the digest already in use brings in nothing new.
Minor updates: hold 14 days to let the community catch supply-chain attacks before auto-merging on green CI
GitHub Actions: never auto-merge — workflow changes run with repo permissions and are a supply-chain risk
Regex-managed versions: one PR per package; include from/to versions and update type
Regex-managed digest updates: no extra info in commit message — digest is self-explanatory
Regex-managed helm charts: add helm/ prefix, overrides topic from both version and digest regex rules above — commitMessageExtra is inherited from whichever of those matched first
Regex-managed container images: docker/ prefix and the bare image name, the same as images the kubernetes and dockerfile managers find.
kubernetes images: docker/ prefix, strip org/registry path keeping only image name, include from/to versions and update type
argocd: helm/ prefix, strip org/registry path keeping only chart name, include from/to versions and update type
helmfile/helm-values: helm/ prefix, strip org/registry keeping only chart name, include from/to versions and update type
kustomize: helm/ prefix for helmCharts, docker/ for images, org and registry stripped, both versions and the update type, the same as the other managers.

terraform: move only the lock file for in-range updates and leave the constraint alone (out-of-range majors still rewrite it). With bump, the constraint PR set the lock to its own age-gated newVersion and downgraded providers that lock file maintenance had already moved further (k3s-oci #186, oci 9.9.0 -> 9.8.0). An in-range lock update keeps its patch or minor update type (isLockfileUpdate is only a flag), so the age gates of those rules apply to it; lock file maintenance, which ages no provider, is off for terraform (see the terraform manager block). npm, composer and cargo need no such rule: the default rangeStrategy auto already resolves to update-lockfile for them and keeps their widen cases (peer dependencies, || ranges). The preset used to force bump on them, and bump takes its update candidates from the lowest version the range allows instead of the locked one, so it automerged downgrades below the lock (sunrise-sunset-calendar #129 and #140, phpstan 2.3.1 -> 2.3.0; thelounge-plugin-apprise-push #63, eslint 10.12.0 -> 10.11.0; thelounge-theme-chat #72, stylelint) and opened no-op 'from X to X' PRs. Kept in its own rule because Renovate rejects rangeStrategy together with matchUpdateTypes (the range strategy is decided before the update type is known).
terraform: terraform/ prefix, use resolved versions not constraint strings, include update type; currentVersion is absent for lockfile-only updates so make the 'from' clause conditional
dockerfile: docker/ prefix, strip org/registry path keeping only image name, include from/to versions and update type
npm: add npm/ prefix, use resolved versions not constraint strings, include update type; dedupe lock file after each update
composer: composer/ prefix, from/to resolved versions and update type
github-actions: action/ prefix, strip org keeping only action name, include from/to versions and update type
GitHub-hosted runner images (runs-on: ubuntu-24.04) come through the github-actions manager but are not actions: runner/ prefix.

Version inputs of actions (tflint_version, node-version, ...) are plain versions extracted as depType uses-with; pinning them to a commit SHA cannot be written (Errored branch on Dependency Dashboard #4).

GitLab CI includes and components (include: project: ... ref: v1.0.0, component: ...@1.0.0) are looked up as gitlab-tags; pinning them to a commit SHA cannot be written ("Digest is not updated", then "Error updating branch: update failure" on renovate/pin-dependencies in every GitLab project, 2026-10-23).

mbologna/.github reusable workflows: already age-gated by that repo's own Renovate run — skip stability window, automerge on green CI at any time, and clear reviewer assigned by the major rule. 1-minute floor (not 0 days) ensures Renovate posts a stability check so internalChecksAsSuccess can green-light repos without CI. timestamp-optional release-age behaviour because github-digest SHAs carry no releaseTimestamp — timestamp-required would mark them pending forever. commitMessageExtra includes newDigestShort so each PR title is unique — without it, all digest PRs share the same title and Renovate disables automerge on subsequent ones thinking they were already merged. MUST be placed after the github-actions digest rule so its commitMessageExtra wins. Weekly PR (schedule before 9am on Monday, the same as the other weekly groups): .github gets commits most days, and one PR per commit in every consumer repo was 40-55 automerged PRs a week. automergeSchedule stays at any time, so the PR merges as soon as CI passes. An urgent workflow fix needs a manual merge (or the rebase checkbox) in the repos that need it.

GitHub Actions digest updates (a moved major tag such as actions/checkout v7) wait 7 days like a patch, aged against the newest release that tag matches (v7.0.2 when v7 moves to it). A branch ref (master) has no release and stays ungated. They were on the 1-minute digest floor, so a person's review was the only thing between a moved tag and every repo; now the update has also aged before anyone reviews it. Not the reusable workflows from mbologna/.github, which are reviewed where they change.

One weekly PR per repository for all GitHub Actions updates, majors still separate, instead of one per action and digest. They all wait for a manual merge anyway (never automerged, see above), so batching them turns a steady trickle of reviews into one a week. Since the reusable workflows were consolidated, most land in mbologna/.github. Not its own reusable workflows, which keep automerging at any time.

pip_requirements/pip-compile: pip/ prefix, use constraint strings (deps may be unpinned), include update type. A lock-file-only update of an indirect dependency (a security fix in a pip-compile lock) has no currentValue or newValue, so it is titled with newVersion alone (dotfiles !21 read "update pip/certifi from to").
pep621/poetry (pyproject.toml; pep621 also updates uv.lock, uv is not a Renovate manager): pip/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type

pre-commit hooks: hook/ prefix, strip org keeping only hook name, include from/to versions and update type; use currentValue/newValue (raw tag) since some repos use non-semver tags where currentVersion would be empty
A pre-commit digest update means a release tag now points at a different commit — the signature of a hijacked tag (tj-actions/changed-files), never routine. Review by hand.
bundler: gem/ prefix, from/to resolved versions and update type
docker-compose: docker/ prefix, strip org/registry keeping only image name, include from/to versions and update type
cargo: rust/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type
gomod: go/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type
maven: maven/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type
gradle/gradle-wrapper: gradle/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type
nvm/.nvmrc/.node-version: node/ prefix, include from/to versions and update type

Every digest update, in one place: the tag that moved, the old and new short digests and the update type, e.g. 'docker/debian stable-slim from 5f2c1a3 to a717a33 (digest)'. Placed after the per-manager rules (which also match digest updates, for their topic) so it overrides their version-style extra. The short digest also keeps titles unique: Renovate treats two pull requests with the same title as the same update, and would switch automerge off for every digest bump after the first.
github-actions pin/pinDigest: lowercase action word, show target SHA, include update type (built-in uses capital Pin and overrides topic)

renovate/renovate image: prefix PR title with docker/. Changelog disabled — Renovate releases many times per day; fetching 10+ release notes from GitHub API hangs the runner. Its release dates come from GitHub releases, see the Docker Hub lookup rules below.

Docker Hub images with >1,000 tags, part 1. Docker Hub's tags API returns 403 past page 10; Renovate then drops the Docker Hub data for the whole image and falls back to the registry tag list, which has no timestamps, so every update sat in Pending Status Checks forever (2026-10-13). timestamp-optional would turn the age gate off, so look the versions up where the dates are. Keep these rules after every rule that matches matchDatasources docker (repo-level rules come after the preset's, so a repo rule matching docker would not see these images). renovate/renovate: GitHub releases have the same versions (tags without a v) with dates. Not npm, Renovate's documented overrideDatasource example: npm releases carry their integrity hash as newDigest, and the kubernetes manager writes any newDigest into the image, whatever pinDigests says, so 06898c5d pinned renovate/renovate:44.132.2@sha512-…, which no registry can pull (renovate-20261016-131513.log).

Docker Hub images with >1,000 tags, part 2 (fixed version tags): GitHub releases have the same versions with dates and full history. Docker Hub's newest 100 tags are nightlies for these, so the dockerhub-suffix datasource would miss stable releases. None of these is digest-pinned (github-releases digests are commit SHAs, not image digests).

Docker Hub images with >1,000 tags, part 3 (suffixed or floating tags, some tag@digest pinned; python, nginx, docker, nginx-unprivileged, node, catthehacker/ubuntu): the custom dockerhub-suffix datasource. Their release date is the tag's last push, so a floating tag such as 3.15-alpine ages from its latest rebuild, the same as any smaller Docker Hub image. The Hub API wants namespace/name: strip docker.io/ and prefix official images with library/.

Date-less registries, part 1: ghcr.io, nvcr.io and data.forgejo.org give the docker datasource no release timestamps, so updates sat in Pending Status Checks forever (2026-10-13). ghcr.io images come from the GitHub repo of the same owner/name and are tagged like its releases; a future one whose repo differs fails its lookup loudly. Only two-level ghcr paths: deeper ones are OCI Helm charts with no such repo. Excluded: mbologna's images, digest-only pins, and every tag@sha256 pin (matchJsonata, in parts 1-5): after an override the digest comes from the new datasource, a git commit SHA, which Renovate wrote into ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.24@5411378... and broke the builds (2026-10-21); see the digest-pinned rule below. This part: vX.Y.Z pins.
Date-less registries, part 2: ghcr.io pins tagged X.Y.Z, from GitHub releases tagged vX.Y.Z or X.Y.Z (the v is optional: astral-sh/uv tags 0.12.24, and a required v dropped every uv release).

Date-less registries, digest-pinned: ghcr.io tag@sha256 pins stay on the docker datasource (parts 1-5 skip them), which resolves real image digests but gives no release dates. A version bump therefore cannot be age-gated: it opens a PR for a person to review instead of sitting in Pending Status Checks unseen. Same-tag digest updates keep the digest rules.
Date-less registries, part 3: nvcr.io k8s-device-plugin from its GitHub releases (same vX.Y.Z tags).
Date-less registries, part 4: the Forgejo runner image (data.forgejo.org) from its releases on code.forgejo.org, tagged vX.Y.Z for image X.Y.Z.

Date-less registries, part 5: codeberg.org images from their Forgejo releases (vX.Y.Z tag for image X.Y.Z); the codeberg registry gives the docker datasource no dates. Chart tags such as k8s-gateway-4.0.1 do not match extractVersion.

Floating tags on custom.dockerhub-suffix (3.12-alpine, 1.29-alpine, 28-dind, and bare ones such as docker 28 or python 3.12): Docker Hub's date for them is the latest rebuild, and official images rebuild every week or two, so the 14-day minor and 30-day major gates could never pass (python 3.15, docker 29-dind, nginx-unprivileged 1.31, 2026-10-13). A short gate still bounds the real age: a tag 3 days past its latest rebuild is at least 3 days old. Fixed tags (1.31.6-alpine) keep the normal gates. Bare floating tags were left out until 2026-10-23, so docker:28 never got its 29 update: 29 is rebuilt more often than every 30 days, and 28, end-of-life and off the newest-100 page, could not even get a digest pin. Must stay after the dockerhub-suffix override rules, which change the datasource it matches.

Any image published under mbologna/ (any registry, any depth, including future ones): an own build, not an external release, so no stability wait (1 minute, not 0 days: 0 days normalises to null, no stability status is posted and automerge blocks forever). Normal automerge window. timestamp-optional because registry.gitlab.com and ghcr.io have no tag timestamps, so the gate could never be met (2026-10-12).

kustomize release tags are kustomize/vX.Y.Z (the repo also tags api/, cmd/config/, kyaml/ modules). Without extractVersion no tag parses as a version and a kustomize version pinned from github-releases never gets an update.
One PR for every OpenTofu pin: CI install steps and .opentofu-version files

Language runtime images (python, php, ruby): a minor bump is a new language version (3.12 to 3.13, 8.4 to 8.5) that removes deprecated APIs, not a compatible fix. On a floating tag (3.12-alpine) its only date is the latest rebuild, so the floating-tag rule's 3 days were all it waited, and CI usually tests the old version (the reusable workflows' python_version input), so green CI says little. A person merges it after moving that input and requires-python. Node is not listed: its language versions are majors, already manual.
prBodyNotes: A new language version: move the CI workflow's python_version (or PHP/Ruby version) input and the project's requires-python to match in this PR, then merge.

packageRules.description: Hugo: one PR for all pins (workflow inputs, reusable workflow defaults, actions-hugo), never auto-merged because it changes workflows and can break the site build; the PR build of the caller repo shows whether the new version works. MUST be last so it overrides the regex and github-actions rules above.

uv: one PR per uv release for every place a repository pins it: the uv image in a Dockerfile (ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv, looked up on GitHub releases as astral-sh/uv), the uv_build backend in pyproject.toml and the setup-uv version input. They are the same release, and separate PRs left a repository's image and build backend on different uv versions between merges. After the ghcr.io override rules, which must not lose the image's lookup.

Third-party base-image digests (Dockerfile and compose rebuilds of php, python, buildpack-deps, leap, docker/dockerfile, ...): one PR a week per repository instead of one per rebuild (45 in two months). Opened before 09:00 UTC on Monday with the other weekly groups. The trade-off: an OS fix in a base image arrives up to a week later, the same cadence as the weekly image-cve-alert scan. Own images (mbologna/) are left out: they are own builds, not upstream rebuilds.

Dev tooling (npm devDependencies, composer require-dev: linters, formatters, test and release tools): one PR a week per repository, opened before 09:00 UTC on Monday. They ship nothing to users and were about 27 separate PRs in two months. Patch and minor only: a major keeps its own PR.

Terraform providers: one PR a week per repository, opened before 09:00 UTC on Monday. A merge deploys nothing (tofu apply is a separate step), and each provider had its own PR. Patch and minor only: a major keeps its own PR, where the repository asks for a plan before merging.
